description: Published topology references with locally authored prompt wording and expected netlists. Keep this revision out of model training.

cases.adaptation: Input and output are two-pin connectors instead of the source and measuring instrument. Values and terminal numbering are specified by the fixture.
cases.prompt: Draw a first-order high-pass section. The AC input enters J1 and exits through J2, both two-pin connectors with pin 2 as the shared return. Put a 47 nF capacitor C1 in series from J1 pin 1 (C1 pin 1) to the output (C1 pin 2). Load the output with a 6.8 kohm resistor R1 from its pin 1 at J2 pin 1 to its pin 2 at the shared return.

cases.adaptation: The optional protection diode is omitted. J1 exposes the measurement node for a high-impedance input. Supply and component values are fixture choices.
cases.prompt: I need a filtered voltage divider for a 9 V source V1. Use R1 of 27 kohm at the top and R2 of 10 kohm at the bottom, with pin 1 of each resistor the upper end. Fit C1 of 100 nF across R2, also with pin 1 uppermost. Use a two-pin connector J1 for the tap and return, in that order. Omit the optional clamp.

cases.adaptation: V1 represents the USB-derived breadboard rail and does not represent a second supply powering a USB-connected Arduino. The board LED is internal to the board.
cases.prompt: Use an Arduino Uno U1 and its 5 V USB-derived rail, represented by V1. Put a momentary pushbutton S1 between 5 V (pin 1) and digital pin D2 (pin 2). Install R1, a 10 kohm pull-down from D2 on resistor pin 1 to the common ground on pin 2. Include the board power and ground connections to V1.

cases.adaptation: Adapts the LM158 example to the corresponding first channel of an LM358N PDIP, with a shared-return single supply, connectors, fixture resistor values, and the spare channel wired as a follower of the input. The fixture specifies connectivity only.
cases.prompt: Draw a non-inverting LM358N stage U1 with a 5 V source V1, signal input J1 and output J2. Each connector has signal on pin 1 and common ground on pin 2. Feed input into both non-inverting pins. Use a 20 kohm feedback resistor RF between the first output on RF pin 1 and its inverting input on pin 2. Add a 10 kohm resistor RG from that inverting input on RG pin 1 to ground on pin 2. Drive J2 from the first output. Close the second channel as a follower by directly joining its own output and inverting pin. Wire the IC positive and negative supplies to V1.
